items.title: Billy Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: Frank Wess and Frank Foster. ... The saxophone section was Charlie Fowlkes on baritone, Frank Wess playing alto and tenor, Frank Foster and myself playing tenor, and Marshall of course.

ctx.x: Who was your other tenor player? Eric Dixon at that time?

No. Eric came in after me. Frank Wess and Frank Foster. Frank alternated playing tenor/ alto, whichever one he had in his hand that’s the one he played. In fact I did it once you get used to it you know. So sometimes, rather than change horns, he would just play his part on whichever horn he had. So whatever struck him. If he felt like playing the third alto part, he’d play it on the alto. If he already had the tenor in his hand, he’d play it on tenor. The saxophone section was Charlie Fowlkes on baritone, Frank…
There certainly was something about the rhythm section in Basie’s group that made it distinctive. Was it enjoyable to play over that rhythm section for the soloists?
